decoder_context: A finite matrix type Matrix ι ι ℝ is the real square-matrix algebra; multiplication is matrix multiplication. Fintype supplies a finite enumeration and DecidableEq supplies equality decisions. Nonempty asserts that the index carrier has at least one element.
Matrix.IsHermitian means conjugate transpose equals the matrix; over ℝ this is transpose equality. Matrix.trace is the ordinary sum of diagonal entries without division by the dimension.

NormedSpace.exp is the power-series exponential in the matrix algebra, whereas Real.exp is scalar exponential. The notation ‖A‖ uses Matrix.Norms.L2Operator, the operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm.
The scalar s ranges over ℝ; |s| denotes the real absolute value. Matrix scalar multiplication multiplies every entry by the displayed scalar.

EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is the n-dimensional real Euclidean space. WithLp.toLp 2 and WithLp.ofLp change representation between coordinate functions and Euclidean coordinates without changing their values.

stdGaussian on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space is its standard centered Gaussian law; Measure.pi forms the displayed finite product law. A displayed Bochner integral uses exactly the displayed unconditional measure.

Matrix.vecMulVec is the outer product of its two displayed vectors. Matrix.kronecker uses a paired index with the first coordinate from the first factor. The if expression uses its displayed inclusive cutoff and actual zero-matrix branch.

Fin d ranges over zero through d−1. The angle formula explicitly adds1. The two universally quantified Boolean values select the displayed deterministic weight and one global scalar sign; they do not name random signs.

Integrable f μ means Bochner integrability of the displayed real scalar function. The ordinary integral notation is the real scalar Bochner integral under μ; a literal integral expression alone does not supply an integrability hypothesis.

reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers d,q ∈ ℕ satisfying 2q + 1 < d, make the following definitions, in the displayed order. Write I_d = {0,…,d−1} for Fin d and J = {0,…,q} for Fin(q+1); when an index occurs in a real formula it means its natural-number value coerced to ℝ.

Let D = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), the real Euclidean space with coordinate carrier I_d, and E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(q+1)), the real Euclidean space with coordinate carrier J. Let Ω = J → D, so ω ∈ Ω assigns one vector ω_b ∈ D to each b ∈ J. Equip Ω with the unconditional measure

    μ = Measure.pi (b ↦ stdGaussian D),

the displayed finite product of the standard centered Gaussian law on D. Let

    M = Matrix (J × J) (J × J) ℝ,
    r = ((q+1 : ℕ) : ℝ),
    L = 2r + 3 log(1000 · (d : ℝ)),
    α_i = ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 − 1/2) · π / (d : ℝ)             (i ∈ I_d),
    t_i(k) = 1                                            if k.val = 0,
             √2 · cos((k.val : ℝ) · α_i)                  otherwise (k ∈ J).

Here log, cos, π and the square root are the real operations appearing in these definitions. Define the Euclidean row vector

    x_i(ω) = WithLp.toLp 2 (b ↦ ω_b(i)) ∈ E.

WithLp.toLp 2 and WithLp.ofLp change only the representation between coordinate functions and Euclidean vectors, preserving all coordinates. For every i ∈ I_d and every ω ∈ Ω define the real matrix Y_i(ω) ∈ M by the literal inclusive cutoff

    Y_i(ω) = (d : ℝ)⁻¹ · [outer(WithLp.ofLp(x_i(ω)), WithLp.ofLp(x_i(ω)))
                          ⊗ outer(t_i,t_i)]              if ‖x_i(ω)‖₂² ≤ L,
             0_M                                         otherwise.

The multiplication by (d : ℝ)⁻¹ is scalar multiplication of every matrix entry. The symbol outer(a,b) means Matrix.vecMulVec a b, with entry a_j b_k. The symbol ⊗ means Matrix.kronecker, with the first coordinate of each paired index coming from its first matrix factor. Thus the nonzero branch has entry, for b,k,b′,k′ ∈ J,

    Y_i(ω)_((b,k),(b′,k′))
       = (d : ℝ)⁻¹ · ω_b(i) · ω_b′(i) · t_i(k) · t_i(k′).

The other branch is the actual zero matrix, and the norm in the cutoff is the Euclidean norm of the row vector. Define

    mean_i = ∫_Ω Y_i(ω) dμ(ω) ∈ M,
    Z_i(ω) = Y_i(ω) − mean_i,

where the mean is exactly the displayed unconditional matrix-valued Bochner integral under μ. For Boolean values useCos and minus define deterministic weights and one global scalar sign by

    w_useCos(i) = cos((((2q+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) · α_i)            if useCos = true,
                  1                                      if useCos = false,
    sign_minus = −1                                      if minus = true,
                 1                                       if minus = false,
    S_useCos,minus(ω) = sign_minus · ∑_{i∈I_d} w_useCos(i) · Z_i(ω),
    Rstar = 2r(L+1)/(d : ℝ).

The sum runs over every i ∈ Fin d. Both multiplications involving w_useCos and sign_minus are matrix scalar multiplications; sign_minus multiplies the entire sum. The Boolean choices are universally quantified deterministic selectors, not random signs.

Then for every real s ∈ ℝ and every useCos,minus ∈ Bool, let

    f(ω) = tr(expₘ(s · S_useCos,minus(ω))),
    B = r² · expℝ(|s| · ((d : ℝ) · Rstar)).

All of the following hold simultaneously:

    (1) f is Bochner integrable as a real scalar function on (Ω,μ);
    (2) for every ω ∈ Ω, 0 < f(ω) and f(ω) ≤ B;
    (3) 0 < ∫_Ω f(ω) dμ(ω);
    (4) ∫_Ω f(ω) dμ(ω) ≤ B.

The pointwise bounds hold for every ω, not only almost everywhere. All displayed integrals use exactly μ. There is no sign or magnitude restriction on s. The trace is the ordinary sum of all diagonal entries indexed by J × J, without division by the dimension; M has (q+1)² rows and (q+1)² columns. The matrix exponential expₘ is the power-series exponential ∑ₙ₌₀^∞ Aⁿ/n! in M with ordinary matrix multiplication; expℝ is the scalar real exponential. A norm of a matrix, if used, has the approved Euclidean operator-norm sense; the norm actually present in this proposition is the Euclidean row norm in the cutoff. No integrability premise is added to the definition of mean_i; the asserted integrability conclusion is specifically Integrable f μ.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.ExpLog.Basic

/-!
# Scalar trace-exponential envelope for finite real Hermitian matrices

The ordinary trace is strictly positive and bounded by the matrix dimension
times the exponential of the absolute parameter times the L2 operator norm.
This is a deterministic canonical library fact for every real parameter;
it does not assert a matrix-valued moment generating function or a tail bound.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix.Norms.L2Operator MatrixOrder
noncomputable section
universe u
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.MatrixTraceExponentialBounds

theorem trace_exp_pos_and_le_card_mul_exp_abs_mul_norm :
∀ {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι],
  ∀ (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ), A.IsHermitian → ∀ s : ℝ,
    0 < Matrix.trace (NormedSpace.exp (s • A)) ∧
      Matrix.trace (NormedSpace.exp (s • A)) ≤
        (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * Real.exp (|s| * ‖A‖)
 := by
  classical
  intro ι _ _ _ A hA s
  have heq : cfc (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (s * x)) A =
      NormedSpace.exp (s • A) := by
    calc
      _ = cfc Real.exp (s • A) :=
        cfc_comp_const_mul s Real.exp A (by fun_prop) hA.isSelfAdjoint
      _ = _ := CFC.real_exp_eq_normedSpace_exp
        ((IsSelfAdjoint.all s).smul hA.isSelfAdjoint)
  have hpos : IsStrictlyPositive (cfc (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (s * x)) A) :=
    (cfc_isStrictlyPositive_iff (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (s * x)) A
      (by fun_prop) hA.isSelfAdjoint).mpr (fun x _ => Real.exp_pos (s * x))
  have htracepos := (Matrix.isStrictlyPositive_iff_posDef.mp hpos).trace_pos
  let C : ℝ := Real.exp (|s| * ‖A‖)
  have hupper : cfc (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (s * x)) A ≤
      algebraMap ℝ (Matrix ι ι ℝ) C := by
    apply (cfc_le_algebraMap_iff (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (s * x)) C A
      (by fun_prop) hA.isSelfAdjoint).mpr
    intro x hx
    apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
    have hnormx : |x| ≤ ‖A‖ := by
      simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using
        IsometricContinuousFunctionalCalculus.norm_spectrum_le A hx hA.isSelfAdjoint
    calc
      s * x ≤ |s * x| := le_abs_self _
      _ = |s| * |x| := abs_mul _ _
      _ ≤ |s| * ‖A‖ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hnormx (abs_nonneg _)
  have htrace := (Matrix.le_iff.mp hupper).trace_nonneg
  simp only [Matrix.trace_sub, Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one,
    Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_one, smul_eq_mul] at htrace
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · simpa only [heq] using htracepos
  · have hle := sub_nonneg.mp htrace
    simpa only [heq, C, mul_comm] using hle

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.MatrixTraceExponentialBounds

lesson.title: Real Hermitian trace-exponential envelope
lesson.statement: For a finite nonempty real Hermitian matrix, the ordinary trace exponential is strictly positive and has the dimension-scaled operator-norm envelope for every real parameter.
assumptions: Let \(\mathcal I\) be finite and nonempty, let \(A\in\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathcal I}(\mathbb R)\) be Hermitian, and let \(s\in\mathbb R\). Real Hermitian means transpose equals itself. No sign restriction on \(s\), norm-cap premise or probability structure is needed for P.

\(\operatorname{tr}\) is the ordinary unnormalized diagonal sum; \(e^A\) is the matrix-algebra power-series exponential, not entrywise scalar exponentiation. The norm is the induced Euclidean/L2 operator norm. Nonempty dimension is essential for a strictly positive trace.

For the private consumer, \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), \(r=q+1\), and \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\) on \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\). The law is the original unconditional product of standard Gaussians; \(q=0\) is included.

For physical rows \(i=1,\ldots,d\), set \(\alpha_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i=(1,\sqrt2\cos\alpha_i,\ldots,\sqrt2\cos(q\alpha_i))\), \(\Phi_i=(\omega_b(i))_{b=0}^q\), and \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). Lean uses the explicit \(i.val+1\) conversion.

\(Y_i=d^{-1}(\Phi_i\Phi_i^\top\otimes t_it_i^\top)\mathbf1_{\{\|\Phi_i\|^2\le L\}}\), \(m_i=\int Y_i\,d\mu\), and \(Z_i=Y_i-m_i\). The cutoff includes equality and uses the same row; the tensor index has Gaussian coordinate first and feature coordinate second, so the matrix size is \(r^2\).

Choose \(w_i=1\) or \(w_i=\cos((2q+1)\alpha_i)\), and a single global \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\). Set \(S=\varepsilon\sum_iw_iZ_i\), \(R_*=2r(L+1)/d\), \(f_s=\operatorname{tr}e^{sS}\), and \(B_s=r^2e^{|s|dR_*}\). For every real \(s\), the consumer concludes \(f_s\in L^1(\mu)\), \(0<f_s(\omega)\le B_s\) for every \(\omega\), and \(0<\int f_s\,d\mu\le B_s\).

All measurability, true-mean compatibility, Hermiticity, radius estimates, probability normalization, cardinality, scalar integrability and positivity are proof ingredients generated internally or obtained by calling canonical producers. They are not extra consumer hypotheses. The two global signs assert no equality of signed laws or MGFs.
lesson.reader_note: Steps1–3 prove the shared deterministic lemma. Steps4–5 are its private material consumer for the four literal signed Gaussian sums.

steps.title: Identify the exponential of the same Hermitian matrix and prove positive trace
steps.text: Apply continuous functional calculus to f_s(x)=exp(sx) for the fixed A. Composition with scalar multiplication identifies f_s(A) with the matrix power-series exponential exp(sA). The scalar function is strictly positive on the real spectrum. Functional calculus therefore gives a positive-definite matrix, whose ordinary trace is strictly positive on a nonempty finite index.

private theorem actual_source_four_trace_mgfs_integrable_positive_and_bounded :
∀ {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d),
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let α : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let tvec : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * α i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω → M := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (tvec i) (tvec i))
    else 0
  let mean : Fin d → M := fun i => ∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ
  let Z : Fin d → Ω → M := fun i ω => Y i ω - mean i
  let w : Bool → Fin d → ℝ := fun useCos i =>
    if useCos = true then Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α i) else 1
  let sign : Bool → ℝ := fun minus => if minus = true then -1 else 1
  let S : Bool → Bool → Ω → M := fun useCos minus ω =>
    sign minus • ∑ i : Fin d, w useCos i • Z i ω
  let Rstar : ℝ := 2 * r * (L + 1) / (d : ℝ)
  ∀ s : ℝ, ∀ useCos minus : Bool,
    let f : Ω → ℝ := fun ω => Matrix.trace (NormedSpace.exp (s • S useCos minus ω))
    let B : ℝ := r ^ 2 * Real.exp (|s| * ((d : ℝ) * Rstar))
    Integrable f μ ∧ (∀ ω, 0 < f ω ∧ f ω ≤ B) ∧
      0 < ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ ∧ (∫ ω, f ω ∂μ) ≤ B
 := by
  classical
  intro d q hq
  dsimp only
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let α : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let tvec : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * α i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω → M := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (tvec i) (tvec i))
    else 0
  let mean : Fin d → M := fun i => ∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ
  let Z : Fin d → Ω → M := fun i ω => Y i ω - mean i
  let w : Bool → Fin d → ℝ := fun useCos i =>
    if useCos = true then Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α i) else 1
  let sign : Bool → ℝ := fun minus => if minus = true then -1 else 1
  let S : Bool → Bool → Ω → M := fun useCos minus ω =>
    sign minus • ∑ i : Fin d, w useCos i • Z i ω
  let Rstar : ℝ := 2 * r * (L + 1) / (d : ℝ)
  let : MeasurableSpace M := borel M
  let : BorelSpace M := ⟨rfl⟩
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := by
    dsimp only [μ]
    infer_instance
  change ∀ s : ℝ, ∀ useCos minus : Bool,
    let f : Ω → ℝ := fun ω => Matrix.trace (NormedSpace.exp (s • S useCos minus ω))
    let B : ℝ := r ^ 2 * Real.exp (|s| * ((d : ℝ) * Rstar))
    Integrable f μ ∧ (∀ ω, 0 < f ω ∧ f ω ≤ B) ∧
      0 < ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ ∧ (∫ ω, f ω ∂μ) ≤ B
  have hstructure :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixStructure.actual_source_centered_matrix_structure
      (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change (∀ j : Fin d, Measurable (Z j)) ∧ iIndepFun Z μ ∧
    (∀ j : Fin d, Integrable (Z j) μ) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin d, (∫ ω, Z j ω ∂μ) = 0) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin d, ∀ ω : Ω, (Z j ω).IsHermitian) at hstructure
  rcases hstructure with ⟨hmeasZ, _, _, _, hhermZ⟩
  have radius :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixRadius.actual_source_truncated_matrix_norm_bounds
      (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change (∀ j : Fin d, ∀ ω : Ω, ‖Y j ω‖ ≤ 2 * r * L / (d : ℝ)) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin d, ‖mean j‖ ≤ 2 * r / (d : ℝ)) at radius

    change ‖Y j ω - mean j‖ ≤ Rstar
    calc
      _ ≤ ‖Y j ω‖ + ‖mean j‖ := norm_sub_le _ _
      _ ≤ 2 * r * L / (d : ℝ) + 2 * r / (d : ℝ) :=
        add_le_add (radius.1 j ω) (radius.2 j)
      _ = Rstar := by dsimp only [Rstar]; ring
  have hw (useCos : Bool) (j : Fin d) : ‖w useCos j‖ ≤ 1 := by
    by_cases h : useCos = true
    · simpa only [w, if_pos h, Real.norm_eq_abs] using Real.abs_cos_le_one
        (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α j)
    · simp only [w, if_neg h, norm_one, le_refl]
  have hnormS (useCos minus : Bool) (ω : Ω) : ‖S useCos minus ω‖ ≤ (d : ℝ) * Rstar := by
    have hsign : ‖sign minus‖ = 1 := by cases minus <;> norm_num [sign]
    change ‖sign minus • ∑ j : Fin d, w useCos j • Z j ω‖ ≤ _
    rw [norm_smul, hsign, one_mul]
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ j : Fin d, ‖w useCos j • Z j ω‖ := norm_sum_le _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ _ : Fin d, Rstar := Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => by
        rw [norm_smul]
        exact (mul_le_mul (hw useCos j) (hnormZ j ω) (norm_nonneg _) (by norm_num)).trans_eq
          (one_mul _)
      _ = (d : ℝ) * Rstar := by simp
  have hmeasS (useCos minus : Bool) : Measurable (S useCos minus) := by
    exact (Finset.measurable_sum _ (fun j _ => (hmeasZ j).const_smul (w useCos j))).const_smul
      (sign minus)
  have hhermS (useCos minus : Bool) (ω : Ω) : (S useCos minus ω).IsHermitian := by
    exact ((IsSelfAdjoint.all (sign minus)).smul
      (isSelfAdjoint_sum _ fun j _ =>
        (IsSelfAdjoint.all (w useCos j)).smul (hhermZ j ω).isSelfAdjoint)).isHermitian

steps.title: Apply P and derive finite positive ordinary scalar expectation
steps.text: Apply P to each actual Hermitian S(ω); its paired index has cardinality r². The pointwise radius gives 0<f_s(ω)≤B_s=r²exp(|s|dR*). Continuity of the matrix exponential and trace, composed with the proved measurable sum, makes the scalar f_s measurable. The deterministic bound on the original probability law yields Integrable f_s. Strict pointwise positivity makes support(f_s)=univ, hence its ordinary integral is strictly positive. Integrating f_s≤B_s and using probability normalization gives ∫f_s≤B_s. Only the scalar trace observable is integrated.
steps.lean:
intro s useCos minus
  let f : Ω → ℝ := fun ω => Matrix.trace (NormedSpace.exp (s • S useCos minus ω))
  let B : ℝ := r ^ 2 * Real.exp (|s| * ((d : ℝ) * Rstar))
  change Integrable f μ ∧ (∀ ω, 0 < f ω ∧ f ω ≤ B) ∧
    0 < ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ ∧ (∫ ω, f ω ∂μ) ≤ B
  have hcard : (Fintype.card (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) : ℝ) = r ^ 2 := by
    simp [r, Fintype.card_prod, pow_two]
  have hpoint (ω : Ω) : 0 < f ω ∧ f ω ≤ B := by
    have hp :=
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.MatrixTraceExponentialBounds.trace_exp_pos_and_le_card_mul_exp_abs_mul_norm
        (S useCos minus ω) (hhermS useCos minus ω) s
    refine ⟨hp.1, ?_⟩
    calc
      f ω ≤ (Fintype.card (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) : ℝ) *
          Real.exp (|s| * ‖S useCos minus ω‖) := hp.2
      _ ≤ (Fintype.card (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) : ℝ) *
          Real.exp (|s| * ((d : ℝ) * Rstar)) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
          (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
            (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hnormS useCos minus ω) (abs_nonneg s)))
          (by positivity)
      _ = B := by rw [hcard]
  have hcontExp : Continuous (NormedSpace.exp : M → M) :=
    continuous_iff_continuousAt.mpr fun A =>
      (NormedSpace.exp_analytic (𝕂 := ℝ) A).continuousAt
  have hmeasf : Measurable f :=
    (Matrix.traceLinearMap _ ℝ ℝ).toContinuousLinearMap.continuous.measurable.comp
      (hcontExp.measurable.comp ((hmeasS useCos minus).const_smul s))
  have hint : Integrable f μ := by
    apply Integrable.of_bound hmeasf.aestronglyMeasurable B
    exact ae_of_all _ fun ω => by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (hpoint ω).1]
      exact (hpoint ω).2
  have hsupport : Function.support f = Set.univ := by
    ext ω
    simp only [Function.mem_support, Set.mem_univ, iff_true]
    exact ne_of_gt (hpoint ω).1
  have hintpos : 0 < ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ := by
    apply (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg (fun ω => (hpoint ω).1.le) hint).mpr
    rw [hsupport]
    simp
  have hintle : (∫ ω, f ω ∂μ) ≤ B := by
    simpa using integral_mono_ae hint (integrable_const B)
      (ae_of_all μ fun ω => (hpoint ω).2)
  exact ⟨hint, hpoint, hintpos, hintle⟩
